source_neutral.procedure: The proposed onboarding redesign is treated as a set of candidate functions mixed together, including suspected dependencies and suspected substitutes. The packet supplies no actual features, no activation definition and no observations. Before any testing, the features, the activation definition, the intended user scenarios and the evidence required to count activation are to be specified. It is provisionally assumed that some functions meet different requirements at different checkpoints and can therefore be told apart; candidates that cannot be separated are kept as bundles instead of being assumed independent. The overall process runs user task attempts through a fixed sequence of activation requirements (checkpoints) in staged prototypes, tracks at each checkpoint the task demand associated with each candidate function, and compares the full proposal against coherent omission variants and pairwise presence/absence variants, under a session budget and task timeout set in advance.
source_neutral.action: 1) Before testing, specify the features, activation definition, user scenarios and required activation evidence. 2) Set a session budget and a task timeout before testing. 3) In staged prototypes, have users attempt the task as they advance through a fixed sequence of activation requirements. 4) At every checkpoint, for each candidate function's associated task demand, record whether the demand is satisfied and the user proceeds, or whether it remains unresolved against that checkpoint's requirement. 5) Repeat this assessment at each checkpoint through the flow, allowing a demand satisfied earlier to become relevant again later. 6) Keep checkpoint criteria, available assistance and scenario conditions comparable across variants, and record any deviations. 7) Compare the full proposal with coherent omission variants; when investigating a failure, restore the omitted function. 8) For suspected pairs, compare four variants: both present, each one present without the other, and neither present, where all four variants remain interpretable. 9) End an attempt at activation, withdrawal or timeout, recording demands that remain unresolved. 10) End the study when the budget is reached and retain unresolved comparisons as uncertain.
source_neutral.observables: Proposed observations, not reported results: the checkpoints and elapsed times at which each demand resolves, recurs or remains blocked; whether activation occurs; errors; and assistance given. Function-associated traces are grouped by where and when they resolve. Groups with distinct patterns are candidate separations between functions; groups with overlapping patterns indicate that the functions may not be distinguishable under the tested conditions. Further observations: whether omitting a function introduces a specific blockage; whether restoring it removes that blockage; and whether the joint presence or joint absence of a pair produces a pattern that differs from the pattern produced by either isolated change.
source_neutral.inferential_warrant: Different trace patterns support the conclusion that the functional demands are distinguishable and depend differently on the tested checkpoints. How long or at which checkpoints a demand persists characterizes its relative persistence under those conditions, not the value of the feature. A function is supported as necessary, for the tested configuration and scenarios and no further, when three conditions hold: a functioning full variant loses activation after the function's coherent omission, the blockage is linked to that omission, and restoration recovers activation under comparable conditions. Successful activation after omission shows the function is dispensable in that tested configuration. Pair comparisons can support complementarity, substitution or order dependence, any of which makes a single context-free feature ranking misleading. Combinations that are uninterpretable or untested support no conclusion about necessity. Observed blockage together with omission/restoration evidence is used to corroborate attribution of a demand to a function.
source_neutral.problem_decomposition: Units: candidate functions of the redesign; the task demand associated with each function; a fixed sequence of activation checkpoints, each with a requirement; user task attempts within specified scenarios; prototype variants (full proposal, coherent omission variants, restoration variants, and four-way pair variants); and bundles of candidates that cannot be separated. Relationships: each function's demand is assessed against each checkpoint requirement as satisfied, unresolved or recurring; functions may be related as dependencies, substitutes, complements or order-dependent pairs; functions may yield overlapping traces because they serve the same requirement, depend on one another, or are measured too coarsely; variants are related by controlled presence or absence of functions with checkpoint criteria, assistance and scenario conditions held comparable. The question of necessity is addressed per function or bundle per tested configuration; the question of what prevents a simple ranking is addressed through the pair comparisons and interaction patterns.
source_neutral.next_inquiry: Specified follow-ups: (a) Before testing, specify the features, activation definition, intended user scenarios and required activation evidence, since the packet supplies none. (b) When investigating a failure in an omission variant, restore the omitted function and observe whether the blockage is removed. (c) If traces overlap, inspect task observations and event traces and, within the declared budget, test a coherent variant designed to separate the overlapping functions; if that is not done or does not separate them, retain the bundle as unresolved. (d) If an omission breaks prototype integrity or changes unrelated requirements, repair that comparison before interpreting it, or mark it uninterpretable. No follow-up beyond the study budget is specified; comparisons unresolved at the budget are retained as uncertain.
source_neutral.limits: Conditions: the features, activation definition, scenarios and activation evidence must be specified before testing; the distinguishability of functions across checkpoints is a provisional assumption; checkpoint criteria, assistance and scenario conditions must be kept comparable across variants with deviations recorded; pair comparisons apply where all four variants remain interpretable; omission variants must be coherent. Stopping rules: an attempt stops at activation, withdrawal or timeout, with unresolved demands recorded; the study stops at its pre-set session budget, with unresolved comparisons retained as uncertain. Inferential limitations: functions may produce overlapping traces because they serve the same requirement, depend on one another or are measured too coarsely; user experience, task order, assistance, prototype fidelity and checkpoint design can shift the apparent persistence of a demand; completion, delay and errors are nonspecific signals that do not identify their cause and do not establish necessity by themselves; necessity and dispensability conclusions hold for the tested configuration and scenarios; uninterpretable or untested combinations support no necessity conclusion; small studies and limited combinations cannot establish population-wide necessity, unique feature identity or a globally minimal activation design. All observations described are proposed, and no results are reported.
